standard_prerequisites: Section construction of the module E: E is the module of equivalence classes of pairs (f, g) with f in k[x, y, z, x inverse, y inverse] and g in k[x, y, z, y inverse], under the equivalence generated by f equals f-prime plus x h modulo y times k[x, y, z, x inverse] and g equals g-prime minus z h modulo y z times k[x, y, z]; the section prose proves (a) multiplication by x is injective on E, (b) multiplication by y is injective on E modulo xE, (c) E over the ideal generated by x and y is zero, and (d) the class of the pair (1, 0) yields a nonzero element delta in E over zE with x delta = y delta = 0
Square-zero extension: for a ring S and an ideal I with I squared zero, the ring S plus I has maximal ideal the sum of the maximal ideal of S and I whenever that sum is an ideal
Localization is exact, so a regular sequence remains regular after localizing at a multiplicative set
core_obligations: Set R equal to k[x, y, z] plus E where E is the module of the section considered as a square-zero ideal

Properties (a), (b), (c) of E give that x, y, z is a regular sequence in R: x is a nonzerodivisor on R, y is a nonzerodivisor on R over xR, and z is a nonzerodivisor on R over the ideal generated by x and y
The element delta of property (d) lies in E over zE inside R over zR, is nonzero, and satisfies x delta = y delta = 0
Localize R at the maximal ideal generated by x, y, z and E: the sequence x, y, z remains regular since localization is exact, and delta remains nonzero because it is supported at that maximal ideal
proof_roadmap: Rebuild the ring as a square-zero extension by the section module E
Read off the regular sequence property from the four properties of E
Check the annihilated element survives localization at the maximal ideal
